record.paper_title: Open problems in the Kontsevich graph construction of Poisson bracket symmetries
record.original_question: Which two-parameter Poisson brackets {·,·}_{a,ρ} on R^3 remain invariant under a fixed Kontsevich infinitesimal symmetry, meaning Q({·,·}_{a,ρ})≡0 at every point? More generally, which Poisson bi-vectors P satisfy both the Jacobi identity [[P,P]]=0 and the invariance condition Q(P)=0 for a chosen symmetry Q?

evidence.quote: Problem 12. Describe those two-parameter Poisson brackets {·, ·}a,̺ on R^3 which stay invariant under a given Kontsevich’s infinitesimal symmetry: Q({·, ·}a,̺) ≡ 0 at all (x, y, z) ∈ R^3. • More generally, describe (classes of) bi-vectors P which are Q-invariant solutions of the Jacobi identity: [[P,P]] = 0 and Q(P) = 0 for a given Q.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let P be a Poisson bi-vector on a smooth affine manifold M, i.e. a bi-vector field P ∈ Γ(Λ²TM) satisfying the Jacobi identity [[P,P]] = 0, where [[·,·]] is the Schouten–Nijenhuis bracket. Kontsevich's graph construction associates to a suitable oriented graph cocycle γ a universal differential-polynomial map P ↦ Q_γ(P) taking a Poisson bi-vector to a bi-vector field on M; for cocycles γ the flow Ṗ = Q_γ(P) is an infinitesimal symmetry of the Jacobi identity, meaning [[P, Q_γ(P)]] = 0 whenever [[P,P]] = 0.

Fix once and for all such a Kontsevich graph symmetry Q (for example, the tetrahedral flow or a pentagon-wheel flow).

Problem. 
(a) On M = ℝ³ with coordinates (x, y, z), consider two-parameter families of Poisson brackets {·,·}_{a,ρ} (depending on parameters a, ρ ∈ ℝ and possibly on the coordinates). Determine all such two-parameter families that are invariant under the chosen Q, in the sense that
   Q({·,·}_{a,ρ}) ≡ 0  at every point (x,y,z) ∈ ℝ³, for all admissible (a, ρ).

(b) More generally, describe all (classes of) Poisson bi-vectors P on ℝ^n (or on an affine manifold M) that are simultaneously
   (i) Poisson:  [[P, P]] = 0,  and
   (ii) Q-invariant:  Q(P) = 0,
for the prescribed Kontsevich graph symmetry Q.
artifact.category_tag: Kontsevich graph flows on Poisson structures
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works (2024–2025) by Kiselev and collaborators on Kontsevich graph flows acting on Nambu–Poisson brackets continue to investigate Q-invariant Poisson structures on ℝ^d (notably for d = 3, 4), and an explicit "Open problems" sequel paper from 2025 still lists the classification of Q-invariant Poisson bi-vectors as an open question. No general classification of two-parameter Q-invariant Poisson brackets on ℝ³, nor of Q-invariant Poisson bi-vectors in general, appears to be available.

status_evidence.title: Kontsevich graphs act on Nambu–Poisson brackets, VI. Open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Open-problems sequel (2025) discussing Q-invariance of Poisson bi-vectors under Kontsevich graph symmetries.
status_evidence.claim: The classification of Q-invariant Poisson bi-vectors under Kontsevich graph symmetries is still listed among open problems.

status_evidence.title: Kontsevich graphs act on Nambu–Poisson brackets, IV
status_evidence.snippet: Studies tetrahedral and pentagon-wheel flows on Nambu-determinant Poisson brackets in dimensions 3 and 4 without giving a full classification of Q-invariant brackets.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist for specific classes (Nambu-determinant Poisson brackets), but no general classification.
